# GridCalc

> A spreadsheet web app that runs entirely in the browser. It has a formula engine written from scratch (lexer, Pratt parser, tree-walking evaluator), dependency-aware incremental recalculation, and a virtualized 100,000 × 100 grid. Errors explain themselves with a caret under the problem and a suggested fix.

- Sheet contents stay in the browser (localStorage). Vercel Web Analytics measures page visits; cell contents and formulas are not sent to analytics.
- 96 built-in functions, including SUM, IF, VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, SUMIFS and TEXTJOIN.
- Local .gridcalc.json backups preserve cell contents and formulas; restore validates the file before replacing the sheet. Values-only CSV export is available separately.
- Circular references are detected and reported as #CIRC! with the cycle path; each cell in the loop is a link and the loop is outlined on the grid.
- Light, dark and semi themes, or follow the system setting; semi keeps the interface dark around a white sheet.
- A first visit opens on a sample sheet with working formulas and intentional errors to fix.
- The status bar counts error cells and jumps between them (F8 / Shift+F8); Ctrl/Cmd + . applies the suggested fix.
- After an edit, the recalculated cells light up in dependency order (a recalculation wave).
